opening.spoken: This record covers the claimed solution of Erdős problem #550: what has been claimed, what it rests on, and what would have to be checked by whom.

short_version.spoken: Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp asked for an upper bound on the Ramsey number of a large tree against a complete multipartite graph in terms of the bipartite case. In June 2026 Eric Li posted a paper claiming the bound for every sufficiently large tree, and in August a Lean development. Nobody independent has reported building the development or reading the argument. Everything here is open.

what_happened.spoken: The claim was pinned from the public record: the problem page, the proof-claims thread, and every artifact the claimants made public, by commit or hash. A reading guide now lays the third-party formal statement and the claimant's own beside the problem as posed, definition by definition, and settles in two lines which reading of "sufficiently large" can be meant, so the human read takes under an hour. Nothing has been built or run. The gaps that follow are the checks still owed.

do_not_rely_on.spoken: the claimed solution as settled; nothing in it has standing yet

certainty_statement.spoken: Nothing is certified or accepted. Every item is open.

cycles.spoken: Eric Li posted the paper on arXiv; the Erdős-problems AI wiki listed it as a candidate full solution, marked unverified. The proof claim was listed on the problem page with links to the paper and a formalisation. The Lean repository was created and reached its current commit, and the paper's second version was posted, the same day. The problem page lists one proof claim, not marked accepted by the site; the repository has no licence file. A third-party formalisation of the problem statement exists.

preregistered.question: Can the open semantic gap (EG2) be made cheaper for a human reviewer: the problem as posed, the third-party and the claimant's formal statements, every definition behind them, a plain rendering, what 'sufficiently large' quantifies, and the points to confirm?
preregistered.rule: Statements quoted verbatim from the pinned files with file and line; renderings marked as the agent's; every discrepancy recorded whether harmless or not; worked examples written as Lean but not run in this cycle, and no output claimed for them; nothing cloned, built or executed; standing unchanged by construction.
predictions: P1: the formal-conjectures statement renders to the page's sentence with k - 1 in place of chi(G) - 1, harmless because every class is nonempty

P2: in both statements the threshold for n depends on k and the class sizes; nothing uniform in G; the page's wording is the sharpest reading question and does not change the meaning in the direction a proof needs
P3: the Ramsey number is the standard non-induced two-colour one; truncated subtraction and sInf of the empty set need a sentence each and change nothing
P4: the claimant's statement and the formal-conjectures statement say the same thing in the agent's reading, but no machine bridge between them exists at the pinned commits

misses: None of the predictions missed. Not done in this cycle: the worked examples and the bridge from the claimant's statement to the formal-conjectures statement are written in cycles/trace-1/Trace.lean and have not been run by Lean; they are pending a run inside the built development (EG1).

cycles.spoken: Nervous Machine wrote the reading guide for the question on this record that a machine cannot settle: whether the formal statements of problem 550 say what Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp asked. The guide quotes the problem page, the third-party formal statement and the claimant's own statement word for word, traces every symbol to its definition in Mathlib or the two repositories with file and line, and gives a plain reading of each piece. Nine conventions are written down; none changes the meaning in the agent's reading. The sharpest is the page's phrase "sufficiently large": both formal statements fix the multipartite graph first and then take every large enough tree, and the guide gives a two-line argument that a threshold uniform in the class sizes would make the inequality false. Sixteen small Lean checks, and a short derivation of the third-party statement from the claimant's, are written but not yet run by Lean. The readings are the system's, not a mathematician's, so nothing changed standing. A graph theorist can now sign or refuse four lines in under an hour.

background.spoken: Let T be a tree on n vertices with n large, and G the complete multipartite graph with class sizes m1 up to mk in increasing order. Show that the Ramsey number of T against G is at most the chromatic number of G minus one, times the Ramsey number of T against the complete bipartite graph on the two smallest classes minus one, plus m1. Chvátal's classical result gives the complete-graph case exactly.

background.spoken: The claim is the stated bound for every sufficiently large n and every n-vertex tree, with k minus one in place of the chromatic number minus one. The proof combines an off-Turán tree-embedding theorem, obtained from Szemerédi regularity and an embedding lemma of Hladký and Piguet, with a compactness-and-rounding theorem for bounded-rank hypergraph obstructions using shadow hypergraphs.
